items.text: M: What are Emma’s favourite stories?
W: When does Emma usually write her stories?

M: Emma, what are you reading now? There are lots of books on your desk.
W: Just some fairy tales. They are my favourite.
M: That sounds great. Do you also write your own stories?
W: Sure. I often write my stories in this notebook.
M: Wow! When do you usually write them?

W: How many students are there in your club?
M: We have twenty students now.

M: Sure. You can join us this Friday.
M: What is the speaker's favorite club?
W: When do they practice in the art room?
M: Who teaches them to move the little people and animals?
W: Where do they usually show their stories?

(W) Traditional arts are very popular in our school. My favorite one is the shadow play club. We tell stories with light and shadow. We practice in the art room every Thursday. We make little people and animals with paper. Mr. Lin teaches us how to make them move like real actors. It is quite amazing and everyone loves it. We usually show our stories on the school stage. Many students come to watch our shows.
M: What are the two goats doing?
W: Where are the rabbits?

W: I love this farm, and I’m so happy to visit it with you guys again.
M: Really? Look, the goats are running around a big box.
W: Yes, they can get water from the box.
M: I want to see the rabbits too. Do you remember where they are?
W: Yes, they are near the farm gate.
M: Great. I hope we can see them later.
M: Where is the young elephant?
W: Why is the young elephant moving her ears?

M: Excuse me, do you work with the elephants here?
W: Yes, I do. How can I help you?
M: I heard there is a young elephant here, but I cannot find her. Where is she?
W: She is standing beside the large rock.
M: I can see her now. Why is she moving her ears so often?
W: Moving her ears helps her keep cool in hot weather.
M: That’s interesting. Thank you for your explanation.
W: You’re welcome.
M: What is Rocky looking for?
W: Who is telling Rocky what to do?

W: Welcome to our rescue dog training centre, and today Rocky will show us part of a rescue dog’s job.
M: Great. What is Rocky looking for among those bags?
W: He is looking for a bag with a special smell.
M: Oh, he is checking all the bags one by one.
W: Yes, his strong nose helps him find the right bag quickly.
M: Who is the man telling Rocky what to do?
W: That is Mr Lee, and he works with the dogs here.
M: I see. We will watch from here and keep quiet.
M: What is the name of the school program?
W: Where is Max leading Ms Green?
M: How does Ms Green make Max start walking again?
W: Why are guide dogs helpful in busy public places?

(W) Today is our school’s Open Day. As part of the “Animal Helpers Program”, the school invites Ms Green, who cannot see, and her guide dog, Max. Ms Green is showing us how Max helps her. He is leading her safely around chairs. When Max sees a bag in their way, he stops. After a student moves it, Ms Green says, “Forward,” and Max starts walking again. Our class claps when they finish. Guide dogs help people walk safely in busy public places. They are not only friendly animals but also helpful partners.

items.text: Plants are a key part of our natural world. We see them everywhere, so tomorrow our class is going to visit a beautiful garden and learn more about these friends. We are going to find out how they help us in many ways. For example, some plants provide food for us, and others give us oxygen to breathe. Some plants can also be homes for small insects. Without them, the world would be very different. I can't wait to explore their magic tomorrow!

Today I am going to plant a sunflower seed in my garden. First, I am going to place the seed gently into the soil. Then, I will water it every day to keep the soil moist. My mum told me it is a long process. A few days later, a small green stem will rise. Gradually, it will grow big leaves to absorb sunlight. Finally, beautiful yellow flowers will come out. What a wonderful experience it is going to be!

A green plant is like a busy factory. First, the roots will send up water. Then, it will rise through the stem to the leaf. The leaf will turn the water, sunlight, and CO₂ into sugar. Another product will be oxygen for animals and humans to breathe. At night, they also take a rest. They work like us, but also give us so much. Because of their hard work, our natural world is full of life!

Welcome to the beautiful forest, a peaceful home for many animals. Look at the river! Some beavers are working together right now. What are they doing? One beaver is cutting down a small tree with its sharp teeth. Some are swimming quickly in the river, while others are trying to build something across the water. It's a dam! People often call beavers nature's engineers. The natural world is full of surprises!

Animals are our fantastic friends, but many of them are in danger. We are losing different kinds of animals every day. To change this situation, scientists are trying to find new ways to help. They do lots of research and put the results into action. For us, there are also lots of things we can do. We can start by protecting their natural homes and saying no to animal products. Even small changes in our daily lives can make a big difference for them.

Henry is studying pigeons for Bird Week. At first, he thinks they are boring and dirty. He watches them in the park and even feels they are scary. Later, he does some research online and finds that pigeons can recognise themselves. He is surprised, so he goes back to the park and sees a pigeon looking at its reflection in the water. He also learns they can fly long distances without getting lost. Now, Henry enjoys watching them because these birds are truly amazing!

In 2017, the new 480-kilometre Mombasa-Nairobi railway was opened.
Before then, the only transport links between Mombasa, Kenya's main port, and Nairobi, Kenya's capital, were rough roads and an old railway line built in 1901.
The old trains were very slow.
It took 10 hours to get to Nairobi from Mombasa by train.
However, the new railway, built with China's help, has already cut the travel time between Mombasa and Nairobi to about four hours for passengers.
Now, more than two million people use it every year.
Local Kenyans have benefited a lot from the new railway.

A government worker said, "I'm very happy with the new railway built by our Chinese friends. Many changes have taken place in the town over the last few years, and the people who live here have become rich."

A businessman said, "My experience of using the train since 2017 has been good. It is very convenient and doesn't cost much money. I am able to get to places on time and make business deals with ease."
The railway has also made the transport of food easier.
"Food used to take hundreds of lorries to carry between the two cities, but now it takes only two or three trains," said a supermarket manager.
As a result, people now have more fresh food to eat.
Although China and Kenya are far away from each other, the railway shows how different countries can work together to build a better world.
Love My Hometown, Build My Hometown
With a deep love for their hometown, people of different ages and professions are contributing to its development and growing along with it.
Today, let us explore three such stories.
The watermelon farmer
Liu Guanghui is an agricultural technology expert in watermelon farming.
Although he is more than 70 years old, he still spends most of his days working in the sun on the farmland.
He wears a wide hat, and his skin is brown from the sun.
He loves farming and has spent his life researching ways to improve it.
On his days off, Guanghui provides local farmers with technical training and guidance for free.
With joint efforts of the government, farmers, and experts like him, the farming economy in the province has grown by more than one billion yuan over the years.
The flower live-streamer
Jiang Hui's friends and fellow villagers call her the "flower girl".
When she was young, Hui often visited her aunt's flower field after school, where she learnt how to grow flowers.
She also showed great talent in putting different flowers together beautifully.
After graduating from university, Hui decided to return to her hometown and start her own flower business.
To promote sales, she started to sell her flowers online.
It was hard at first, but she didn't give up.
She always patiently explained and offered practical advice to customers.
Gradually, her online shop became more popular.
She also helped and taught other villagers how to sell agricultural products online.
"Many people now know about the agricultural products from our town," Hui said with a big smile.
"This makes all the hard work worthwhile!"
The village teacher
When Yuan Bailing was a little girl, it took her almost an hour to get to school each day, but she loved school so much that she never missed it.
As she grew up, she witnessed how her village changed greatly over the years.
Better roads and bridges have been built.
Now it takes only ten minutes for children to get to school.
As the first person from her village to graduate from university, Bailing decided to return to her hometown to become a teacher.
She wants to help more children get a good education and be part of her hometown's growth and development.
Though the area still needs further development, through the courage and hard work of its people—like Bailing—it has a bright future ahead.
